user.title: Push Alert TTS (unofficial Pushover client)
user.description:
Registers Home Assistant as a new device on your Pushover account so it receives a copy of every alert. Your phone and computer are not affected.

Pushover counts this as a desktop device: it needs a Pushover for Desktop licence (US$4.99 once-off) after a 30-day trial.

This integration is not made or supported by Pushover.

data_description.device_name: How this device appears in Pushover. Letters, numbers, _ and - only, max 25 characters.
data_description.store_password: WARNING: the password is saved in PLAIN TEXT in Home Assistant's storage (.storage/core.config_entries) and in backups. Only needed if you want the integration to log in again by itself. Not possible if your Pushover account uses two-factor authentication. If off, the password is used once and forgotten.

init.title: Push Alert TTS settings
init.description: Choose where and how alerts are spoken. Changes apply immediately.

data.wake_wait: Wait for speakers to wake up (seconds)
data.announce_retries: Retries if an announcement fails or is cut short
data.part_max_length: Maximum length of each template part
data.word_replacements: Word replacements for the normal text (optional)

data_description.speakers: Media players to announce on. All selected speakers speak at the same time. Separate speakers can start a second or so apart; use a speaker group below to keep them in sync.
data_description.speaker_group: A speaker group (e.g. a Google Home speaker group) that contains the speakers above. The announcement plays on the group so every speaker starts together; volume is still set and put back on each speaker. If the group is unavailable, fails or doesn't start playing within 10 seconds, each speaker is used instead. Leave empty to turn this off.
data_description.preconnect_group: With a speaker group, only the group is woken, once, before an announcement (never each speaker on its own). On: wake it as soon as an alert arrives, while it is still being worded, so the announcement starts a few seconds sooner. Off: wake it when the announcement starts. Same single connect sound either way.
data_description.wake_wait: Only without a speaker group: before speaking, wait up to this long until every speaker above is awake, so a speaker that was off doesn't miss the start. It speaks anyway when the time is up. 0 = don't wait. (With a group, the group is woken once and its speakers are waited for up to 10 seconds.)
data_description.announce_retries: If the speakers won't play the announcement, never start playing or stop much sooner than the text needs, play it again up to this many times (0-5). When every try fails, the fallback notification is sent. 0 = off (speakers that never report 'playing' would otherwise hear each alert twice).
data_description.tts_entity: For example Google Translate or Home Assistant Cloud.
data_description.tts_backup_entity: Used when the main voice can't make the audio after all its tries (see below), and for playback retries, so a slow or broken voice service can't stop the alert. A voice that works without the internet (such as Piper) is best. Leave empty to use only the main voice. The Language setting applies to the main voice only.
data_description.tts_language: Leave empty for the engine's default, e.g. en-GB.
data_description.tts_timeout: Seconds the main voice may take to make the audio, per try. Be generous: a short delay is better than a missed alert. Default 20.
data_description.tts_retries: If the main voice fails or is too slow, try it again this many times (for example on a poor internet connection) before the backup voice is used. The backup voice starts making its audio as soon as the main voice fails a try or is slow, so it is ready by then; the main voice is still preferred until it has used every try. Default 3.
data_description.tts_backup_voice: The backup engine's own voice, if it has several. For Piper, for example en_GB-cori-high or en_GB-cori-medium (see Settings > Voice assistants, or the Piper add-on, for the names). Empty = the engine's default voice.
data_description.tts_backup_timeout: Seconds the backup voice may take to make the audio. Local voices on a Raspberry Pi can be slow (a 'high' Piper voice can take over 30 seconds for one sentence on a Pi 4). Default 120.
data_description.regex: Used when 'What to say' is set to the regex option. Without a template it speaks the named group called say if your pattern has one, otherwise group 1, otherwise the whole match. Case-insensitive, and '.' also matches line breaks. If nothing matches, the fixed phrase is spoken. See the README for ready-made patterns.
data_description.max_length: Characters. Longer text is cut at a word. 0 = no limit (a hard limit of 2000 always applies).
data_description.app_filter: Comma-separated Pushover application names. Empty = all apps.
data_description.fallback_notify: Notified if a speaker is unavailable, the Pushover connection drops, or login is needed. E.g. notify.mobile_app_your_phone.
data_description.offline_alert_delay: Seconds the Pushover connection must be down (while enabled) before warning.
data_description.regex_source: Which part of the alert the regex searches, in order. The first match wins.
data_description.spoken_template: Regex mode only. Builds the sentence from your regex's named groups: write each group's name in curly brackets, e.g. Alert, then the name host in curly brackets. Also available: app, title, message, priority, priority_name and group numbers. Empty groups are skipped; if fewer than half are filled the fixed phrase is spoken instead. See the README for examples.
data_description.part_max_length: Characters. Each template part is cut at a word to this length, so one long value can't take over. 0 = no limit.
data_description.tidy_text: Reads underscores as spaces, dots between words (host.name) as spaces and | as a pause, and removes doubled or dangling commas.
data_description.expand_abbreviations: Speaks common IT shorthand in full, e.g. prod as production, db as database, lb01 as load balancer 01. Whole words only. The full list is in the README.
data_description.remove_repeated_words: Spoken template only. Leaves out words an earlier part of the sentence already said, so names repeated in an alert are only spoken once.
data_description.history_days: Days. Saves every received alert to a small file in your config folder so you can look back with the get_history action. 0 = off (and deletes the saved history).
data_description.word_replacements: One per line, written as: from = to. For example Re-Triggered = re alert. Whole words or phrases, any capitals. Applies to the normal (non-AI) spoken text only; to change the AI's wording, use the AI instructions or memory. Empty = off.

delivery.name: Combining and delivery (optional)
delivery.description: Speak alerts that arrive together as one announcement, keep the speakers ready between them (fewer connect sounds and volume beeps), check that important speakers really played each alert, and send a notification when they didn't. Everything here is off until 'Combine alerts' is switched on; then alerts are spoken as before except where described. See the README.

data.missed_bell: Also show missed alerts in Home Assistant

data_description.combine_alerts: On: everything to be said goes into one queue. The speakers are woken and set to the announcement volume once, alerts that arrive together are said as one announcement ('3 alerts have arrived. First alert: ...'), and alerts that arrive while it is speaking follow straight after ('2 more alerts have arrived ...'). One alert on its own is said exactly as before. Off = each alert is announced on its own, as before.
data_description.gather_seconds: When the first alert arrives, wait this long for others before speaking, so alerts arriving together are said together. Emergency alerts never wait. 0 = speak at once. Default 3.
data_description.stay_connected: After speaking, keep the speakers awake at the announcement volume this long before putting them back, so alerts that follow soon after don't cause another connect sound or volume beep. 0 = put them back straight away. Default 60.
data_description.must_hear_speakers: Speakers that must play every alert (they must also be in the speakers list above). After each announcement, each one is checked; one that didn't play it hears it again on its own, starting with 'Missed alert TTS:'. If it still didn't play, each alert is sent to the fallback notification (with its link). Empty = no check.
data_description.night_must_hear_speakers: Used instead of the list above while the night condition is true (for example only the bedroom speaker). Empty = always use the list above.
data_description.night_condition: A template that is true at night, for example: {{ is_state('sensor.phone_battery_state', 'Charging') and is_state('media_player.bedroom_tv', 'on') }}. Empty = never night. If it can't be worked out, it counts as day.
data_description.link_label: The text before the link to open from a notification, as it appears in your alerts, e.g. Monitor Status for Datadog alerts (the words Monitor Status followed by the link). The link is never spoken. If no such link is found, the alert's Pushover link is used when it is a web link. Empty = Monitor Status.
data_description.missed_bell: When a must-hear speaker didn't play an alert, also add a Home Assistant notification (the bell in the sidebar) with the alert and its link.

ai_wording.name: AI wording (optional, local LLM)
ai_wording.description: Let a language model you run yourself (for example Ollama on a PC) word each alert as one short sentence. If it is off, slow, unreachable or answers badly, the normal text above is spoken instead, so no alert is lost. See the README for setup.

data.ai_timeout: Wait for the AI at most
data.ai_keep_alive: Keep the model loaded for (Ollama, optional)
data.ai_start_pattern: AI answer must start with (optional regex)
data.ai_auto_backfill: Re-word missed alerts when the AI is back
data.ai_offline_alert: Repair alert when the AI is unreachable for

data_description.ai_enabled: Off = alerts are spoken exactly as before.
data_description.ai_api: Ollama, or any server with an OpenAI-compatible chat API (LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM, LocalAI, OpenAI).
data_description.ai_url: For example http://192.168.1.50:11434 for Ollama, or http://192.168.1.50:1234/v1 for LM Studio.
data_description.ai_model: The model name exactly as the server lists it, e.g. qwen3.5:9b.
data_description.ai_api_key: Only if your server needs one. Saved in Home Assistant's storage.
data_description.ai_timeout: Seconds. If there is no usable answer in this time the normal text is spoken. If the server could not be reached, the AI is skipped for the next minute so alerts are not held up.
data_description.ai_emergency_timeout: Seconds. Emergency (priority 2) alerts wait at most this long, so they are always announced promptly.
data_description.ai_max_words: Answers much longer than this (more than about one and a half times) are not used.
data_description.ai_context_size: Ollama only. The num_ctx the model is loaded with, in tokens. 0 = the server's default. If other programs use the same model with a different context size, Ollama reloads the model each time the caller changes, which can add 15-20 seconds. Set this to the same value they use to avoid that.
data_description.ai_gpu_layers: Ollama only. How many of the model's layers go on the graphics card (num_gpu). Empty = Ollama decides; 0 = CPU only. Like the context size, Ollama reloads the model when this differs from the copy already loaded, so match what other programs use.
data_description.ai_keep_alive: Ollama only. How long the model stays in memory after an alert, e.g. 10m, 1h, or -1 for always. Empty = the server's default (5 minutes unless changed). Set this to match other programs so an alert does not shorten their setting.
data_description.ai_instructions: What the AI is told before each alert. {max_words} is replaced by the number above. Leave as is if unsure.
data_description.ai_start_pattern: A regular expression the answer must match at its start, e.g. ^(P\d alert|Alert) at . Other answers are not used. Empty = any speakable answer.
data_description.ai_memory: Plain-language corrections sent with every alert, e.g. Say HAProxy as HA proxy. You can also add lines with the AI correction box or the add_ai_memory action. Earlier versions are kept in the config folder.
data_description.ai_auto_backfill: When the LLM server answers again after being unreachable, alerts that got the normal text meanwhile are worded by the AI for the AI review list (nothing is spoken). Same as running the reprocess_ai action.
data_description.ai_offline_alert: Minutes. Shows a Home Assistant repair when the LLM server has not answered for this long; it clears itself when the server is back. The server is checked every 5 minutes (a plain web request; no model is loaded). 0 = off.
data_description.ai_wake_entity: A button, input button or script that wakes the PC running the LLM, e.g. a Wake on LAN button. It is pressed when the server stops answering, at most once every 10 minutes while it stays unreachable.
data_description.ai_backup_url: A second LLM server, used only when the main one can't be reached, within the same time limit. Same server type and API key as above. Empty = no backup.
data_description.ai_backup_model: The model name on the backup server. Empty = the same model as above.
data_description.ai_backup_condition: Any entity; the backup is only used while it is on (for example a laptop that should only be used on mains power). Empty = whenever needed.

error.regex_required: Enter a regular expression, or choose another mode.
error.invalid_notify: Use the form notify.your_service_name, for example notify.mobile_app_your_phone.
error.unknown_placeholder: The template uses a name that your regex does not capture and is not built in. Check the spelling, or add a named group to the regex.
error.group_in_speakers: Pick the speaker group here only, not also in Speakers. Speakers should list the individual speakers in the group.
error.template_without_regex: A spoken template only works when 'What to say' is set to the regex option.
error.ai_url_required: AI wording is on: enter the LLM server address, starting with http:// or https://.
error.ai_model_required: AI wording is on: enter the model name.
error.ai_invalid_pattern: The 'AI answer must start with' pattern isn't a valid regular expression.
error.ai_invalid_keep_alive: 'Keep the model loaded for' must be empty, a whole number of seconds (-1 = always), or a duration such as 30s, 10m or 1h.
error.must_hear_not_speaker: Must-hear speakers must also be selected in the speakers list.
error.invalid_night_condition: The night condition is not a valid template.

login_failed.title: Push Alert TTS needs you to log in to Pushover again
login_failed.description: Pushover rejected the saved session. Open the integration and re-authenticate.

device_stopped.title: Push Alert TTS has stopped receiving alerts
device_stopped.description:
{reason}

Fix the cause on pushover.net, then reload the integration (Settings > Devices & services > Push Alert TTS > three dots > Reload).

ai_offline.title: Push Alert TTS: the AI is unreachable
ai_offline.description: The LLM server at {url} has not answered since {since}. Alerts are still spoken with the normal text, so none are lost. Check that the PC running it is on and awake. This clears itself when the server answers again; missed alerts are then re-worded for the AI review list if that option is on.

acknowledge.name: Acknowledge
acknowledge.description: Acknowledge pending emergency Pushover alerts (stops re-alerting on all your Pushover devices) and stop speaker repeats.

speak.name: Speak
speak.description: Say a message on the configured speakers at the announce volume.

get_history.name: Get alert history
get_history.description: Return saved alerts, newest first. Turn on Keep alert history in the integration options first.

days.name: Days
days.description: Only alerts from the last this many days. Default: the whole kept history.

limit.name: Limit
limit.description: Maximum number of alerts to return.

search.name: Search
search.description: Only alerts whose title, message, app or spoken text contains this (not case-sensitive).

preview.name: Preview spoken text
preview.description: Show what would be spoken for an alert with the current settings, and optionally say it. Handy for testing a regex or template.

last_alert.name: Use last alert
last_alert.description: Start from the last alert received. Fields below override it.

app.name: App
app.description: Pushover application name to test with.

speak.name: Speak it
speak.description: Also say the result on the configured speakers.

use_ai.name: Use AI wording
use_ai.description: Also ask the AI (if AI wording is on). Off = only the normal text.

add_ai_memory.name: Add AI memory
add_ai_memory.description: Add a plain-language correction to the AI memory. It is sent to the AI with every alert from now on.

text.name: Correction
text.description: For example: Say HAProxy as HA proxy. Several lines add several corrections.

get_ai_memory.name: Get AI memory
get_ai_memory.description: Return the AI memory (one correction per line), also numbered for remove_ai_memory.

reprocess_ai.name: Re-word past alerts with AI
reprocess_ai.description: Ask the AI to word past alerts that got no AI text (for example while the AI was offline), so you can review and correct them. Nothing is spoken; what was spoken at the time stays recorded.

limit.name: Limit
limit.description: Maximum number of past alerts to word in one run.

remove_ai_memory.name: Remove AI memory
remove_ai_memory.description: Remove a correction from the AI memory, by its number (get_ai_memory lists them numbered) or its exact text.

text.name: Text
text.description: The exact text of the line to remove.

add_ai_correction.name: Add an AI correction for an alert
add_ai_correction.description: Save a plain-language correction to the AI memory, with the alert it is about, then word that alert again (nothing is spoken) so you can check the result. Used by the review card's Improve? button.

text.name: Correction
text.description: What the AI should do differently, in plain words.

received.name: Alert received
received.description: The alert's received time, from the AI review list or get_history.

title.name: Alert title
title.description: The alert's title, if you don't have its received time.

reword.name: Word it again
reword.description: Ask the AI to word the alert again with the new memory and return the result. Nothing is spoken.

no_last_alert.message: No alert has been received yet, and there is no saved history to take one from.

preview_nothing.message: Give a title and/or message, or turn on Use last alert.
